title: The Hockey Stick Galaxy
caption: The Hockey Stick Galaxy, NGC 4656, imaged by the Hubble Space Telescope
celestial: NGC 4656 · constellation Canes Venatici · about 30 million light-years away (source figure)

recognition.text: ESA/Hubble Picture of the Week (an editorial selection, not an audience score).

story: This Hubble picture zooms in on the bright central region of NGC 4656, a galaxy found in Canes Venatici, the Hunting Dogs. From this partial view you would never guess that it is nicknamed the Hockey Stick Galaxy.

Seen in full, the galaxy is stretched into a long, warped stick that curls around at one end, rather like the blade of a hockey stick. This framing captures only the middle, so the curl lies outside the picture.

The odd shape is thought to come from interactions with a couple of close neighbors, the Whale Galaxy, NGC 4631, and a small elliptical called NGC 4627. When galaxies pass near each other, gravity can pull their gas, stars and dust into distorted new arrangements, completely reshaping them. Hubble has photographed many such interacting systems over the years.
scale: Using the source's listed field of view (2.76 x 2.58 arcminutes) and distance (30 million light years), the frame spans roughly 24,000 × 23,000 light-years. Its light set out about 30 million years before reaching the telescope.

understand.summary: This image comes from Hubble's Wide Field Camera 3, using filters from the ultraviolet through visible light to near-infrared, including a hydrogen-alpha filter. The color assigned to each filter is not published.
understand.eye: Some of the light captured, in the ultraviolet and near-infrared, is invisible to the eye, and the long exposures gather far more light than an eye could.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: Other interacting galaxies Hubble has captured include Arp 273, which resembles a rose, and Arp 142, whose pair looks like an egg next to a penguin.
alt: A close view of the bright central region of an elongated galaxy.
